newsitem.title: INDONESIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indonesian newspapers - May 2.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indonesian newspapers - May 2.

text.p: The following are the leading stories in the Indonesian press on May 2. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

The government-backed faction of the Indonesian Democratic Party (PDI) staged campaign rallies in the capital Jakarta amid tight security to prevent the gatherings from being disturbed by people who claim to be supporters of the party's ousted leader Megawati Sukarnoputri.

President Suharto has denied rumours that he will remarry. Suharto's wife, Tien, died of a heart attack last year. There have been rumours that Suharto will marry a younger sister of Pertiwi Hasan, wife of timber tycoon Bob Hasan.

The foreign ministers of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) will hold a special meeting next week in Kuala Lumpur to discuss the admission of Cambodia, Laos and Burma into the group as full members.
Petrochemical giant PT Tri Polyta is planning to build a $300 million propylene plant capable of producing between 300,000 and 500,000 tonnes annually.
